_comment: CTF-P1b — THE REGIONS OF AN AGENT HARBOR STORY, NAMING NO RENDERER'S LAYOUT.
Each region is one part of a story's drawing — the view, its frame's title
tab, the head and the rows of a panel or list, the active tab, the +N chip,
the '+' control, a hover popup, an open dropdown, a loading / empty / error
notice — and says which element it is in EACH renderer, in that renderer's
own terms: `web` is a CSS selector over the web views' classes (the first
visible match in document order, `document.querySelector`), `gpui` the
`data-ah-*` facts the GPUI views put on the element (every one present; a
non-empty value must match exactly). It is read by both capture paths and
transcribed into neither: `tools/visual-review/capture-storybook.mjs
--regions` (the browser's `getBoundingClientRect`) and `codetracer-gpui-story
--regions` (GPUI's own layout, read back through isonim-gpui's
`layout_bounds`). Where it is laid out is each renderer's own answer.
A region a story does not draw is absent from both sides' answer; a region
one side draws and the other does not is a failure of
`test_ctf_p1b_gpui_capture_matches_web_layout`, which compares the two
answers with PLAT-35's pane-rectangle comparator (`layout_questions
.compareAnswer`, `PaneRectangleTolerancePp`: 2 hundredths of the viewport
per edge, never raised).
A region marked `fill` is also checked for its BACKGROUND, which no layout
answer carries: the web capture records the colour the browser composites
behind the element (its own background over its ancestors'), and the layout
test reads the GPUI frame's pixel 4px in from the region's right edge, half
way down -- inside the element's padding, clear of its text -- against it.
The ROW regions (`*-first`, `*-last`) are single rows of a list: the first
one, and (`"pick": "last-whole"`) the last one drawn whole, its bottom
edge inside the viewport. A list compared as one block keeps its outer box when every
row inside it is drawn a few pixels taller, so the rows drift down unseen;
the first row's height and the last visible row's position catch that
drift. A region with a `pick` also reports its `index` among the visible
matches on both sides, and the layout test requires the two to agree: two
different rows that each sit near the bottom of their window can be within
the tolerance of each other by position alone.
`milestone-bar` and `milestone-legend` are the first milestone bar drawn
and the counts beside (or, labelled, under) it. A bar can be the wrong
width while the row around it keeps its box: the web gives the legend
`min-width: 9rem` so the bars of all rows end together, and a view that
did not drew its bar about 70px wider.
A region with `px` (a list of its edges among `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`) is also
compared on those edges IN PIXELS, to within `PxTolerance` (2px) of the
web's, on top of the pane-rectangle comparison, which it does not replace.
Two hundredths of a 1440px viewport are 29px: a tab 9px narrower than the
web's, an error reason on 19px lines instead of 16px, a head 8px short or a
notice running into the strip's 8px inset all pass it. These regions are
the ones whose size the views compute themselves (the single-line tabs'
Flexbox shrink, the inbox position's minimum, the strip notice's budget,
the error reason's line pitch, the list head's rows, the docked summary's
offset; the initiative bar's tabs, `+N` and "+", the `bar-*` regions,
whose places follow from the inactive tabs' widths; and a tab bar's
`caption`, whose height follows from its lines), so a pixel-level answer
is the one that can fail.
`bar-overflow-menu` is the initiative bar's `+N` menu alone (`menu` is
whichever dropdown is open). It hangs from its chip, `bar-overflow`: the
layout test holds its right edge to the chip's on each side, shifted only
as far as the window requires. `strip-overflow-menu` and `strip-overflow`
are the session strip's menu and chip, held to the same rule.
`bar-active-tab-label`, `-progress` and `-recordings` are the initiative bar's
active tab's title, its `n/m` and its recording buttons. They are compared as
pane rectangles only, not in pixels: GPUI sets each run of text in a box its
width rounded up to a whole pixel, so a row of runs differs from the browser's
by up to a pixel a run. What must agree exactly is whether the title is cut
(`elision`, below): two hosts can give the tab the same width and still cut
its title in one and not the other. `playback-readout` and
`playback-moment` are the story hosts' playback bar's readout and the moment
it names, whose width (`px`) is what the bar left it: a moment cut to two
letters on one side, or dropped, is a different width from the whole one.
A region with `elision` is a line of text, and each side also reports whether
it is cut (`cut`: its words wider than its box; the browser measures them
with a Range, GPUI from the width the view says they take, `data-ah-text-px`).
`same`: cut on both sides or on neither -- a box can be the same width on
both sides within every tolerance and still cut the words on one (a 0.2px
shortfall elides a title). `never`: cut on neither side.
The `timeline-*` regions are the session activity timeline's (CTF-P2b): its
list (`timeline`), its first and last line, its first group line, its first
open line, the focused line, the `N new` chip, the `Running:` strip and the
filter row. A region with `within` counts only the matches drawn wholly
inside the first element of that selector on each side (a scrolling list):
the browser lays out every line of a list and scrolls it, GPUI draws only
the lines its list shows, so a line scrolled out of the list's box is no
match on either side. The line regions are `fill` regions too: a line sits
on the panel's ground, with nothing behind it (the timeline is cardless).
The omnibox composer (CTF-P2c) adds its own: the field in the caption bar,
the sheet under it, the sheet's header line and its send button; its
`surface` is the story's whole window (`.ah-composer-story`), as the GPUI
view's root is.
